==Problem==
How many different real numbers <imath>x</imath> satisfy the equation <cmath>(x^{2}-5)^{2}=16?</cmath>

<imath>\textbf{(A) }0\qquad\textbf{(B) }1\qquad\textbf{(C) }2\qquad\textbf{(D) }4\qquad\textbf{(E) }8</imath>

==Solution 1==
We have that <imath>(x^2-5)^2 = 16</imath> if and only if <imath>x^2-5 = \pm 4</imath>. If <imath>x^2-5 = 4</imath>, then <imath>x^2 = 9 \implies x = \pm 3</imath>, giving 2 solutions. If <imath>x^2-5 = -4</imath>, then <imath>x^2 = 1 \implies x = \pm 1</imath>, giving 2 more solutions. All four of these solutions work, so the answer is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(D) }4}</imath>. Further, the equation is a [[quartic Equation|quartic]] in <imath>x</imath>, so by the [https://artofproblemsolving.com/wiki/index.php/Fundamental_Theorem_of_Algebra Fundamental Theorem of Algebra], there can be at most four real solutions.

==Solution 2==
We can expand <imath>(x^2-5)^2</imath> to get <imath>x^4-10x^2+25</imath>, so now our equation is <imath>x^4-10x^2+25=16</imath>. Subtracting <imath>16</imath> from both sides gives us <imath>x^4-10x^2+9=0</imath>. Now, we can factor the left-hand side to get <imath>(x^2-9)(x^2-1)=0</imath>. If <imath>x^2-9</imath> and/or <imath>x^2-1</imath> equals <imath>0</imath>, then the entire left side will equal <imath>0</imath>. Since the solutions can be both positive and negative, we have <imath>4</imath> solutions: <imath>-3,3,-1,1</imath> (we can find these solutions by setting <imath>x^2-9</imath> and <imath>x^2-1</imath> equal to <imath>0</imath> and solving for <imath>x</imath>). So, the answer is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(D) }4}</imath>. Note: every positive root can also be shown as negative

==Solution 3== 


Subtract 16 from both sides and factor using difference of squares: 



<cmath>(x^2 - 5)^2 = 16 </cmath>
<cmath>(x^2 - 5)^2 - 16 =0 </cmath>
<cmath>(x^2 - 5)^2 - 4^2 = 0 </cmath>  
<cmath>[(x^2 - 5)-4][(x^2 - 5) + 4] = 0</cmath>
<cmath>(x^2 - 9)(x^2 - 1) =0 </cmath>
<cmath>(x+3)(x-3)(x+1)(x-1) = 0. </cmath>


Quite obviously, this equation has <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(D) }4}</imath> solutions. 


~TaeKim
